title: SLO Escalation and Proactive Capacity Circuit Runbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook describes the SLO escalation circuit and an automated, telemetry-driven capacity intervention (the "Proactive Capacity Circuit") designed to reduce time-to-remediation for SLO burn and prevent large-scale degradations. It complements existing emergency throttles and postmortem procedures by enabling measurable, reversible capacity moves before customer-impacting thresholds are reached.

Intended audience: on-call SREs, platform engineers, capacity planners, and responsible incident commanders.

Scope and objectives

- Scope: multi-tenant inference services (text-generation, embedding) served from the Redwood runtime. Applies to hosted and dedicated capacity pools.
- Objectives:
  - Detect sustained SLO burn trends earlier than hard SLA breaches.
  - Automate safe capacity adjustments (scale-up / shift / escrow release) when confidence is high.
  - Provide explicit manual escalation steps when automation abstains or fails.
  - Preserve cost guardrails and rollback safety for customer-facing workloads.

Definitions and roles

- SLO-owner: team that defines the service SLO.
- On-call SRE: first responder owning the runbook execution.
- Capacity steward: platform engineer authorized to alter reserved pools and capacity escrow policies.
- Incident commander (IC): leads communications and cross-team coordination if escalation passes threshold.

Signals and thresholds

Primary telemetry signals (inputs to the circuit):
- SLO burn-rate (1h, 6h, 24h windows)
- Error-rate by class (5xx, model-timeout, kv-cache-miss)
- Latency p50/p90/p99 and tail slope (delta over baseline)
- Queue length and backlog by tenant priority
- Model hot-pool utilization and GPU memory pressure
- Autoscaler headroom fraction and scaling latency
- Synthetic canary latency and correctness checks

Threshold table (operational):

| Signal | Warning | Actionable | Emergency |
|--------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 1h SLO burn rate | > 1.2x expected | > 1.5x expected -> automate if confirmed | > 2.0x expected -> manual escalation |
| p99 latency delta | > +25% | > +50% -> run proactive circuit | > +100% -> emergency degrade |
| Queue length | > 60% sustained growth | > 100% growth | queue > capacity -> eviction flow |
| GPU memory pressure | 70% | 85% | 95% |

Note: thresholds are tuned per-service and must be published on the service’s SLO page.

Confidence gating and noise reduction

Before automation triggers:
1) Correlate signals across three independent sources (service telemetry, autoscaler metrics, and synthetic canaries).
2) Validate that the burn persists for at least two consecutive evaluation windows (configurable; default 5m windows, 3 consecutive).
3) Ensure no ongoing scheduled maintenance or deployment that explains the spike.
4) Run a light-weight replay of recent requests in the staging harness (if available) to reproduce the tail behavior.

Proactive Capacity Circuit design (high level)

Overview: a decision pipeline that executes safe capacity actions with automatic rollback and operator notifications. The circuit has three modes: Observe, Intervene-Automated, and Intervene-Manual.

Components:
- Signal aggregator (telemetry-rule-engine) — computes composite burn score.
- Decision engine — evaluates policy and risk profile; supports abstain, propose, execute decisions.
- Capacity actuator — APIs that can (a) release capacity escrow, (b) increase autoscaler target limits, (c) shift model routing to regional pools, (d) instantiate temporary burst nodes.
- Safeguard layer — rate-limits actions, enforces RBAC, runs pre/post smoke checks.
- Audit & evidence store — captures telemetry snapshot, decision logs, and execution traces for post-incident review.

Automated actions and safety limits

Action types (each action emits a ticket and Slack/PagerDuty notification):
- Release escrow chunk: incremental release of reserved capacity (default chunk: 10% of reserved pool, max 40% per 6h).
- Autoscaler upshift: temporarily increase min nodes by X (default X = 1 node) and raise target concurrency.
- Route degrade to lower-cost model variant for low-priority tenants (TTL-based).
- Start hot-pool workers in warm mode (no model reload) to reduce spin-up latency.

Safety limits (hard-coded):
- Max automated cost delta per-account: $500/hr (configurable per contract).
- Max automated capacity increase per-cluster: 25% sustained over 1h.
- Any capacity action that crosses a customer SLA or contractual reservation requires a manual approval by a capacity steward.

Automated circuit decision flow (concise):

1) Telemetry-rule-engine computes composite burn = weighted(SLO burn, p99_delta, queue_growth, canary_fail_rate).
2) If composite burn > 0.7 (actionable) and confidence gates pass, decision engine proposes action(s).
3) Decision engine runs simulated smoke checks (synthetic traffic to new resources) and risk score.
4) If risk score <= threshold: execute action with 15-min monitoring window.
5) If any smoke check fails or risk exceeds threshold: escalate to on-call for manual intervention.

Manual escalation flow (when automation abstains or fails)

Steps for On-call SRE (ordered):
1) Acknowledge PagerDuty alert and open the runbook incident in the incident tracker.
2) Confirm telemetry: pull dashboards for the last 1h, 6h, 24h and attach evidence to the ticket.
3) Check deployment and maintenance windows for coincident events.
4) If confident, execute a controlled capability release: call /api/v1/capacity/escrow/release?amount=<percent> (see CLI examples below).
5) If automated actions exist but failed, inspect decision logs in /internal/slo-circuit/decisions; capture the decision payload and attach to the ticket.
6) If action succeeded but SLO continued to burn, coordinate with IC to perform:
   a) tenant priority gating (move non-critical tenants to degraded path),
   b) emergency model variant switch, or
   c) emergency cold-eviction per tenant SLO contract.
7) Close or hand off the incident after verification and a 1-hour stability window; record post-action telemetry.

CLI and API examples

- Release escrow chunk (curl):
  curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/capacity/escrow/release" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"pool":"us-west-1-inference","percent":10,"reason":"proactive-circuit-triggered"}'

- Increase autoscaler floor (alpha):
  redwoodctl autoscaler set --cluster us-west-1 --min-instances 6 --comment "proactive-circuit temp upshift"

- Smoke check script (pseudo):
  #!/bin/bash
  for i in 1..50; do echo "request $i" | curl -sS -X POST https://synth-canary.internal/generate; done | grep -q "OK"

Decision matrix (example)

- Composite burn 0.7-0.85 + risk <= 0.2 -> automated escrow release (10%) and start hot workers.
- Composite burn 0.85-1.1 + risk <= 0.15 -> propose autoscaler upshift + escrow release (15%); require on-call approval within 10m.
- Composite burn >1.1 or risk >0.4 -> abstain automation; immediate manual escalation to IC.

Communication templates (for rapid use)

- Slack alert (brief):
  [SRE] Proactive Capacity Circuit triggered for service inference-api-usw1. Composite burn=0.88. Proposed actions: escrow-release 15%, autoscaler-upshift +1. Waiting on on-call approval. Ticket #RED-12345.

- Customer-facing status blurb (when IC opens status):
  We are observing elevated latency for inference APIs in US-West. We are running proactive capacity interventions to reduce impact. No data loss is expected. Next update in 15 minutes.

Post-action verification and rollback

- Verification: observe SLO burn, p99 delta, and queue length for 15 minutes post-action. If metrics improve and stabilize for 30 minutes, mark action as successful.
- Rollback triggers:
  - Unexpected error-class increases tied to new nodes (e.g., model-mismatch) -> rollback immediate.
  - Cost breach alarm triggered -> rollback and escalate to finance oncall.
- Rollback steps: reverse changes in reverse order (autoscaler floor back to prior, drain and terminate burst nodes, re-allocate escrow). Always run smoke checks after each rollback step.

Evidence capture and incident review guidance

- Every circuit activation must create an evidence bundle with: telemetry snapshot, decision payload, API call traces, smoke check results, and operator notes.
- Tag incident review with label: slo-circuit-activation. Use the post-incident template and attach the evidence bundle.
- Review cadence: Monthly SRE review of all automated activations — focus on false positives, cost impact, and opportunities to tighten confidence gating.

Operational tooling and dashboards (must-haves)

- Composite burn dashboard: 1h/6h/24h views with service drilldowns.
- Decision log UI: searchable by service, time, action, and outcome.
- Action audit timeline: shows action start/stop, smoke checks, and rollback events.
- Cost impact estimator: predicted cost delta before executing an automated action.

Runbook maintenance and ownership

- Owner: Capacity steward team (primary), eng-sre (secondary).
- Review cycle: this runbook must be reviewed quarterly and after any automated activation that required manual rollback.
- Playbook updates: include parameterization for per-service thresholds; store canonical thresholds on each service SLO page and reference them from the decision engine.

Appendix A — Per-service quick checklist (for on-call)

1) Confirm alert and attach dashboards.
2) Check for deploys/rollouts in the last 30m.
3) Check autoscaler health and recent scaling events.
4) Validate canary responses.
5) Execute escrow release or autoscaler upshift as described.
6) Monitor 15-60 minutes and escalate if no improvement.

Appendix B — Risk assessment questions (to decide manual approve):

- Will this action materially change customer billing or reserved capacity? (Yes -> higher approval)
- Are the affected tenants high-priority / contractual? (Yes -> escalate to IC)
- Can we rollback within 15 minutes with automated steps? (No -> manual intervention required)

Related documents

- See service-specific SLO pages for exact thresholds and list of protected tenants.
- See capacity-escrow-policy for contractual limits and finance approvals.

Contact and escalation list

- SRE escalation channel: #sre-ops
- Product escalation: product-oncall@redwood.internal
